fact: A decree by Prime Minister Aldabaiba made e-payment an approved method for collecting state revenues and public dues, requiring Ministry of Finance treasuries and other ministries, departments and agencies to accept it alongside cash and cheques.
The Libyan prime minister said the government has adopted electronic payment as the official means of collecting government fees and dues.
The Central Bank of Libya made e-payments mandatory for all private and public revenue collectors, according to Libya Herald.

Ministry of Finance Decision No. 247 of 2024 approves electronic collection as a method for paying income tax and directs the Tax Authority to prepare the infrastructure, under Central Bank of Libya electronic payment controls.
The Libya Observer reports the economy minister and the Commercial Registry Authority discussed the rollout of an e-payment system for fees and the issuance of digital receipts.
The Ministry of Finance said the Unified Tax System launch implements Decision No. 448 of 2025 on digital transformation and tax e-payment and e-collection, with digital platforms to launch in 2026.
